module_summary: src/init.c is the IOP driver manager of the EE ELF: it imports the embedded IRX blobs, tracks which modules are resident (have_* flags), loads driver stacks lazily on first path access (USB/BDM, ATA, HDD/PFS, DVR, MMCE, MX4SIO, iLink, PC CARD CF, network/SMB/NFS/UDPFS/FTP/SMBD, keyboard), switches mutually exclusive stacks by IOP reset (Reset, resetRuntimeDeviceState, switch*Stack), prepares special IOP sessions for the KELF signer (exploit IOPRP) and the Ember USB handoff, and owns poweroff handling and a bounded fileXio stat RPC. include/kelf_signer.h is the small public API of src/kelf_signer.c (header/system constants and three functions), all of which are used by src/main_exploit_installer.c.

reusable_helpers.name: fileXioGetStatBounded
reusable_helpers.what: fileXio GETSTAT through a private NOWAIT RPC client with a timeout, so a wedged device cannot freeze the caller

reusable_helpers.name: waitForUsbMassPath
reusable_helpers.what: polls a USB/mass path with bounded stats until it answers or a 2 s deadline passes

reusable_helpers.name: loadExternalFile
reusable_helpers.what: reads a whole file from any device path (mass/hdd/dvr/cdfs/generic) into a memalign'd buffer

reusable_helpers.name: isPathDeviceStackLoaded
reusable_helpers.what: reports whether a device path can be accessed without loading drivers or resetting the IOP

reusable_helpers.name: emberUsbIdentifyFile
reusable_helpers.what: file identity from size plus FNV-1a hash of the first 512 bytes

reusable_helpers.name: setFileXioTransferWide
reusable_helpers.what: sets the fileXio RW buffer to 128/64/16 KB with fallback

findings.title: init.c keeps #else branches for EXFAT and HOMEBREW_SIO2MAN, which every build defines
findings.problem: ps2.yaml:623 and :629 always define HOMEBREW_SIO2MAN and EXFAT, and scripts/configure_ds34.py (the only other build config) copies them unchanged. So the non-EXFAT paths (classic usb_mass driver, busy-loop delay(), mass:/massN: Ember remount names, MX4SIO/iLink fallbacks, loadPcCardCfModules stub) and the rom0:SIO2MAN/PADMAN + MC_TYPE_MC paths are never compiled. The non-EXFAT branch could not even link: usb_mass_irx is not in the ps2.yaml embed list (only usbmass_bd_fork is).
findings.fix: Delete the #ifndef/#else branches and the #ifdef EXFAT / #ifdef HOMEBREW_SIO2MAN guards in init.c, keeping the defined-path code (and simplify pathUsesUsbMass line 1706 to the bare mass: test once the numbered-slot early return is unconditional). Other files that test these macros belong to other units. Tests that grep for '#ifdef EXFAT' (tests/test_ember_two_usb_handoff.py:112-129 and similar) need the matching edit.
findings.benefit: ~100 source lines removed (about 62 lines of dead #else bodies plus ~40 guard lines, counted from the cited ranges); no ELF change because the preprocessor already drops them (INFERRED)
findings.evidence: Grep HOMEBREW_SIO2MAN|EXFAT over *.yaml,*.yml,*.py,*.sh: defined only at ps2.yaml:623 and :629; configure_ds34.py:34-39 only adds DS34 and ds34 targets. Grep usb_mass in ps2.yaml: only iop/usbmass_bd/src/usb_mass.c source (line 194), no usb_mass embed; usb_mass_irx referenced only at init.c:84,1796,2097. All cited branches read in init.c.

findings.title: load_ps2atad_stack, have_ps2atad and the ps2atad_irx embed are dead (function marked unused, no caller)
findings.problem: load_ps2atad_stack is declared and defined with __attribute__((unused)) and nothing calls it; have_ps2atad is set only inside it, so the test at line 549 and the reset at 3034 only ever see 0. Its ps2atad_irx import is the only user of the 'atad:ps2atad' embed, which the linker already garbage-collects. The function also carries a second copy of the hddarg/pfsarg tables from load_ps2hdd_stack (lines 752-769 vs 687-705, the duplicate-block lead).
findings.fix: Delete load_ps2atad_stack and its prototype, the ps2atad_irx import, the have_ps2atad flag and its two uses, and the 'atad:ps2atad' line in the ps2.yaml embed list.
findings.benefit: ~62 lines removed; no shipped-size change: BUILD-EVIDENCE.md says ps2atad_irx (11,477-byte payload) is already garbage-collected (MEASURED); one fewer embed step per build
findings.evidence: Grep load_ps2atad_stack|have_ps2atad|ps2atad_irx over the whole repo: init.c:93,215,386,549,749,776-781,800,3034 only (no test, no other source). ps2.yaml:683 'atad:ps2atad'. evidence/Launchstation/BUILD-EVIDENCE.md:103,121,131: ps2atad_irx.o .data discarded by --gc-sections.

findings.title: switchPsxHddDriverStack does nothing in release builds (only early returns and DPRINTF)
findings.problem: The body of switchPsxHddDriverStack only tests flags and returns, or calls DPRINTF, which launchelf.h:164 defines as empty in shipped builds. It changes no state and loads nothing, so its two calls in loadHddModules and loadDVRPHddModules are no-ops. Its name suggests a stack switch that was removed.
findings.fix: Delete the function, its prototype and both calls (with the #ifdef DVRP wrapper around the call in loadHddModules).
findings.benefit: ~25 lines removed; the static function is probably already inlined to nothing, so no measurable ELF change (INFERRED)
findings.evidence: Read init.c:2329-2347 in full: no assignment or call except DPRINTF. launchelf.h:157-165: DPRINTF empty unless SIO_DEBUG/POWERPC_UART/COMMON_PRINTF/UDPTTY, none defined by ps2.yaml. Grep switchPsxHddDriverStack: init.c:387,2330,2667,2719 plus a conditional string check in tests/test_pccf_owner.py:97 ('if boundary in body'), which still passes after removal.

findings.title: Debug-build macros IOPTRAP, UDPTTY, POWERPC_UART (cannot link), SIO_DEBUG and NO_IOP_RESET are set by no build
findings.problem: No ps2.yaml target or script defines any of these. IOPTRAP, UDPTTY and POWERPC_UART load ioptrap_irx, udptty_irx and ppctty_irx, which exist nowhere in the repo or embed list, so turning them on fails to link; UDPTTY plus POWERPC_UART together would also redeclare 'int i, d' inside Reset(). SIO_DEBUG and NO_IOP_RESET still compile but are unmaintained leftovers: NO_IOP_RESET removes the IOP reset that every stack switch in this file depends on. The two SIO_DEBUG blocks at 1244-1251 are back to back.
findings.fix: Delete the IOPTRAP, UDPTTY and POWERPC_UART blocks (imports and load code) and the matching lines in the info screens. Either delete SIO_DEBUG and NO_IOP_RESET too, or if they are kept as a debug option, merge the two SIO_DEBUG blocks into one.
findings.benefit: ~25 lines removed in init.c plus ~25 in the two info screens; no ELF change (preprocessor-only code, INFERRED)
findings.evidence: Grep -i IOPTRAP|UDPTTY|POWERPC_UART|SIO_DEBUG|NO_IOP_RESET|ioptrap|udptty|ppctty over src/Launchstation: only init.c, dash_info.c, main_info_screens.c, include/launchelf.h, docs/changes.txt, and iop/vmcman (its own SIO_DEBUG); no hit in ps2.yaml, scripts or workflows. Glob **/*{tty,trap}*: no IRX files. Reset() declares 'int i, d;' at both 3080 and 3086.

findings.title: emberUsbProbePath only builds a string for a stripped DPRINTF; its checks repeat emberUsbSourceIsUsb
findings.problem: prepareEmberUsbHandoffIop calls emberUsbProbePath to fill probe[MAX_PATH], whose only reader is the DPRINTF at 2065 (empty in shipped builds). Its path validation (usb:, usbN:, mass:, massN:) is already done by emberUsbSourceIsUsb(ember_path) on the next line, which is stricter (it also checks the BDM driver name).
findings.fix: Delete emberUsbProbePath, the probe buffer and its call; log ember_path in the DPRINTF instead.
findings.benefit: ~43 lines removed and one MAX_PATH stack buffer less in prepareEmberUsbHandoffIop (INFERRED from the cited lines)
findings.evidence: Grep emberUsbProbePath: init.c:1831 (definition) and 2053 (only call). probe is read only at 2065 inside DPRINTF; launchelf.h:164 makes DPRINTF empty for release. emberUsbSourceIsUsb (1919-1953) accepts exactly usb:/usbN: and mass:/massN: (with a driver-name check under EXFAT), a subset of what ProbePath accepts. Grep probe|ProbePath in tests/test_ember*.py: no hits.

findings.title: loadUsbModules re-implements loadBdmCoreModules inline
findings.problem: Lines 1765-1780 load bdm_irx then bdmfs_fatfs_irx with the same have_bdm/have_bdmfs latching as loadBdmCoreModules (2465-2481), which loadMx4sioModules, loadIlinkModules, loadPcCardCfModules and loadAtaBlockDriver already use. The only difference is two extra 'USB BDM'/'USB BDMFS' loading messages.
findings.fix: Replace the inline block with 'if (!loadBdmCoreModules()) loaded_ok = 0;' and drop the two extra messages ('USB core IO' is already shown at 1750).
findings.benefit: ~13 lines removed; a few dozen bytes of .text (INFERRED)
findings.evidence: Read both blocks: same SifExecModuleBuffer calls, same (ID >= 0 && ret >= 0) latching, same order. Grep loadBdmCoreModules: init.c:381 prototype (visible before 1765), callers 2404,2444,2492,2516. Grep 'USB BDM' in tests: no hits.

findings.title: prepareExploitSignerIop repeats its post-reboot re-init sequence in both branches
findings.problem: The failure branch (849-859) and the success path (864-874) run the same seven steps: SifInitRpc, SifLoadFileInit, initsbv_patches, clearIopModuleState, iop_reset_generation++, ensureCoreIoStackReady, DS34 load, setupPad. The success path only adds SifIopSync and clearing the PCCF ownership first.
findings.fix: Do the SifIopSync and PCCF clear only when ret > 0, then run the shared re-init once, then return 0 if ret <= 0, else load SECRSIF as now.
findings.benefit: ~9 lines removed (INFERRED from the cited ranges)
findings.evidence: Read init.c:821-882. tests/test_pccf_owner.py:101-103 requires SifIopSync to come before 'pccf_bus_owned = pccf_loaded = 0' in this function, which the restructure keeps.

findings.title: init.c clutter: prototypes repeated from init.h and commented-out code
findings.problem: loadUsbModules, ensureCoreIoStackReady, setupPowerOff, startKbd, Reset and closeAllAndPoweroff are declared again at 365-369 and 392 although init.h (included at line 2) declares them at init.h:10,19,27,29,30,31. Lines 1255, 1258, 1369-1370 and 3095 are commented-out code (rom0 MCMAN/MCSERV loads, ESR case labels, setupPad).
findings.fix: Delete the six repeated prototypes and the five commented-out lines.
findings.evidence: Grep of the six names in include/: init.h:10,19,27,29,30,31 (loadUsbModules also launchelf.h:759). init.c:2 includes init.h. Commented lines read directly.
